plate.narration: In MossHome, a tree door swings open above a mat of welcome moss. A bigfoot archivist waits with an armful of knotted cords. Root stairs twist upward behind her. This town keeps its stories in surprising places.

objectives.label: Read the spiral in the path archive
Earned the trust of MossHome's record

goal.text: Find out what the forest town remembers, then climb out to the foothills.

steps.label: Climb up out of the forest

facet_confiscated.name: The Confiscated Stone
facet_confiscated.text: The loudest stone in the forest's pile. MossHome's record knows who is carrying it.

knot_cord.name: MossHome Knot-Cord
knot_cord.text: Old bigfoot knots that say the record knows you. Show it when the forest pays back.

scene_mosshome.narration: Your job: find out what MossHome, the forest town, remembers, then climb out to the foothills. Houses grow inside trees here. A leaning chair has a sign: FILE OPENED. A bigfoot runner jogs past. "Archive first! Wipe your feet!" She does both without stopping.

scene_mosshome_feet.narration: You wipe your feet on the welcome moss by the archive door. Then you wipe them again. The door flies open. "Twice!" breathes an archivist. "Nobody from outside wipes twice." She lets you straight in.

scene_mosshome_glade_word.narration: You mention the glade. The archivist at the door runs her thumb along a cord to a knot. "That glade's record changed this morning. It got better." She beams. "In. Feet."

scene_mosshome_ask_door.narration: Your bigfoot knocks on the archive door three slow times, the MossHome way. The door opens by itself. An archivist drops an armful of cords. "Nobody's done that in years. Come in. Wipe your feet."

check_archive_door.narration: The archivist folds her arms on the doorstep. "Don't tell me your road," she says. "Show me. Every path that moved under your boots."

interaction.cue: Everybody act out a piece of your road, until the archivist's eyebrows go up.

options.label: Stomp a squelchy marsh
options.reaction: Squelch, squelch. The archivist's eyebrow twitches.

options.label: Splash across a river
options.reaction: Splash! A drop lands on the archivist's clipboard.

options.label: Tiptoe past grumpy thorns
options.reaction: You tiptoe so well that the moss holds its breath.

onSuccess.narration: You stomp the last bend of your road into the moss. The archivist's eyebrows go up, and up again. "Come in. Wipe your feet. Twice."

onFailure.narration: You stomp the wrong way and sit down hard in the moss. "Wait on the bench," says the archivist. The bench is still growing. Slowly, it lifts you to the window.

scene_archive_table.narration: Every forest path that ever moved is drawn on the archive's great tree-slice table. Fresh thorns mark this season's changes. There are so many that an archivist has put her tea on the floor.

scene_archive_table_read.narration: Your bigfoot reads the table the MossHome way, one finger along the moss-ink, humming each path's name. The finger goes around, and around, and around again. The shape is already there.

scene_archive_table_newest.narration: The archivist points to fresh thorns: a folding path, a hedge holding prospectors, a beech sitting across the way. "Somebody walked those this week." She looks at your boots. The welcome moss missed a spot.

check_plot.narration: The archivist hands you yarn and a fistful of thorns. "Three paths moved in the first week. Pin them in the order they moved, and the shape will show itself."

interaction.cue: Share your clues, then pin the three moved paths in the order they moved.
clues: The river path moved first, on the morning of the big rumble.
The tree path moved after the marsh path.

onSuccess.narration: Thorn, yarn, thorn, yarn, and slowly a shape comes out of it.

onFailure.narration: You tangle the yarn so badly a cat would be embarrassed. An archivist untangles it and shows you the shape anyway.

scene_spiral.narration: On the table, the moved paths are not random at all. They spiral around every place a stone fell, like bathwater down a drain. Every path bends away. The woods are not flinching from the mountain. They are flinching from the stones.

scene_spiral_on.narration: "Before?" The archivists look at each other. One goes to the back of the archive. Soon you hear slow footsteps coming, and a small bird singing.

scene_spiral_hum.narration: You hum the note the stones hum. Every archivist stops. A spool of cord rolls under the table, and nobody chases it. "The oldest knots were tied to that note," one whispers, and sends for the oldest archivist.

scene_spiral_pin.narration: You pin the road you walked onto the table. It brushes the edges of several spirals. The archivists check each bend, then send for the oldest archivist.

scene_spiral_charm.narration: You move the witch's charm over the table. Over the middle of every spiral it rings: ding, ding, ding. Between them it is silent. The archivists go pale and send, quickly, for the oldest archivist, who hates being hurried.

scene_knot_cords.narration: The oldest archivist brings knotted cords in a box. A bird nests in his beard, so he walks very slowly. "The paths flinched like this long ago," he says. "The forest has kept the record all along. The stones are older than the mountain's name."

scene_knot_cords_rest.narration: You thank him. "Did not ask what the forest keeps," the oldest archivist tells a cord, a little too loudly. The door archivist sighs and turns you back.

scene_pile_question.narration: The forest keeps a pile under its roots: tools, hats and humming gems it took from diggers. "The pile is the forest's," says an archivist. "The record decides who it trusts."

check_trust.prompt: Tell the archivists, honestly, what you want the stones for

onSuccess.narration: They listen to the whole thing. Then they all write something down at once, and the oldest one nods.

onFailure.narration: "The record doesn't know you yet," says the archivist, kindly, and closes the box. Maybe it will, by the time you're further north.

scene_pile_visit.narration: In a root hollow lie picks, sieves, three hats and humming gems. One stone sings louder than the rest. "That one wants north," says the archivist. "Carry it if you like. We will record who has it."

scene_pile_visit_leave.narration: You leave the loud stone where the forest put it. The archivist ties a small knot in a cord anyway. "The record will remember that too," she says. Behind you, the pile hums on in the dark.

scene_pile_visit_carry.narration: You lift the loud stone out of the pile. It hums against your chest like a cat that has decided you will do. The archivist ties a small knot in a cord. "North," she says. "That's all it wants."

scene_pile_sneak.narration: Your kitsune slips after the archivist like a shadow with a tail, down a root-stair into a hollow of picks, hats and humming gems. One stone sings louder than the rest. Nobody is watching, except maybe the forest.

scene_pile_sneak_leave.narration: Your kitsune looks at the loud stone a long moment, and leaves it there. On the way back up, a root moves aside to make the step easier. It did not do that on the way down.

scene_pile_sneak_pocket.narration: Your kitsune pockets the loud stone with the smoothest hand in the realm. Then every root in the hollow creaks at once, softly, like a very large person clearing its throat. Nobody saw. The forest saw.

scene_leaning_chair.narration: Back in the square, the chair from the sign still leans away from the archive's root-stairs. A small archivist measures it with string and sighs. FILE OPENED, says the sign.

check_chair_sit.narration: You sit in the chair and lean back hard. It stands upright while you sit. The moment you stand, it leans away again, like a sunflower turning. The archivist writes under FILE OPENED: STILL OPEN.

scene_leaning_chair_follow.narration: The chair leans away from the root-stairs behind the archive, the ones that go down into the dark. The small archivist sees you looking. She goes and stands in front of the stairs, humming.

rest_guest_tree.narration: Rest in the guest tree. Its hammocks hum when you rock them. In the morning, the MossHome elders want to hear what you found. Nearby, the runner ties the day's news cords, feet jogging even while she sits.

rest_guest_tree_knot.narration: The runner teaches you a knot: over, under, twist, pull. It is strong enough to hold a bridge plank. When yours holds, she cheers so loudly a hammock wakes up and hums at her.

rest_guest_tree_hammock.narration: You rock a hammock, and it hums a slow lullaby like rain on leaves. You mean to rock for just a minute. When you wake, it is morning, and there is moss tea on a shelf beside you.

scene_runners_post.narration: On the way to the elders, runners jog in place at their hollow-stump post with news from the other roads. "First question's yours!" puffs the runner. One runner has tied a reminder cord around a banana.

scene_runners_post_rush.narration: "The rush road?" A runner puffs out the news. A ford line two days long. A witch whose charms ring by themselves. Cinder wolves that won't sleep near gem wagons. "Same shape as here," she says. "Everybody's noticing."

scene_runners_post_river.narration: "The river road?" A runner wipes his brow. The troll at Stone Crossing asks one question now: where did you get that, and where is it going? Out east, the manticore prides bend their roads around something. "Everybody's noticing," he puffs.

scene_runners_post_gullet.narration: "Gullet?" A runner laughs. "Notched hat, hums a lot?" Gullet has run out of hat and started on her other hat. "She says she's not worried," he puffs. "Which means she is."

scene_cloud_gatherer.narration: Near the elders' ring, a young dragonling sits in a patch of cloud, her gathering bag beside her. "Not lost," she says. "Grandmother sent me to the elders." Embermoths drift south past her. She stares. "They never go that way."

scene_cloud_gatherer_walk.narration: On the way, she teaches you the one rule: "Take what the mountain drops. Never pry at what it holds." She says it twice. "Grandmothers say it at every boundary stone. Nobody listens this year."

check_follow_moths.prompt: Keep up with a drifting flock of embermoths through the trees

onSuccess.narration: You follow them, the gatherer at your heels, to the edge of town, where the whole flock has settled on a fence. Every single moth is facing away from the mountain, like people with their backs to a cold draft. "I'm telling my grandmother," the gatherer whispers. Then she leads you back to the elders' ring.

onFailure.narration: The moths vanish into the trees, glowing, and you lose them. Then they come drifting back past you the other way, as if they have changed their minds, and then change them again. "Even they don't know where to go," says the gatherer, and leads you back to the elders' ring.

scene_cloud_gatherer_greet.narration: Your dragonling touches a claw to their brow: "What the mountain drops, we keep. What it holds, we leave." The young gatherer lights up. "You're from the foothills!" She tells you her town's bell tower is the tallest anywhere.

choice_elders.narration: The MossHome elders sip tea in a ring of stumps. "Somebody must hear what you found," says the eldest. "The Skywardens, the guards in silver and violet at Redspire Citadel, write everything down. The dragonling grandmothers in the foothills ring the bells." She sips. "Tell whoever you like first. Only tell us second." Who will you tell? Everybody vote.

choice_elders_close.narration: "Nobody yet," says the eldest, and looks at you over her cup a long time. "Careful is a kind of telling, too." She sips. "When you do tell. Second."

choice_elders_gatherers.narration: "The grandmothers," says the eldest, and for the first time all evening she smiles. "Bells carry further than cords." She sips. "Tell them we said so. And tell us second."

choice_elders_wardens.narration: "The wardens," says the eldest. "They write things down. That is not nothing." She sips. "Second," she reminds you. Every elder nods at once, and every cup of tea ripples.

scene_runner.narration: The runner gives you a knotted cord: the forest's receipt for your visit. "Show it when the record needs to know you." Then she jogs away, already late for something she never stopped doing.

scene_falls_stair.narration: Water covers the falls stair. A bigfoot flood-warden in tall boots needs help. "Pass me logs, and I'll teach you a brace for the high path. Or watch the runoff, and learn where a dropped pack would wash." Her boot holds a surprised frog.

check_falls_logs.prompt: Everybody drag heavy stepping logs across the flooded stair

onSuccess.narration: Heave, roll, heave, and three logs settle across the flooded steps like a little bridge. The flood-warden stamps on each one, hard, and nods. "Proper work," she says, which from a flood-warden is a medal. You cross with dry boots, and she waves you up toward the high paths.

onFailure.narration: A log rolls the wrong way and you sit down in the falls with a splash. The flood-warden hauls you out with one hand, sets you on the top step, and says, "Happens every season. Not usually to this many." Then she drags the logs across herself, as if they weigh nothing at all.

scene_falls_stair_count.narration: Grumble, rise. Quiet, fall. You watch the water with the flood-warden. Runoff collects in three fern pockets below the high path, a good place to look if a pack slips. She ties the pockets into your cord.

scene_falls_stair_dripping.narration: "The flooded paths?" The flood-warden grins. "You're the soggy ones! The whole forest heard!" She laughs a big bigfoot laugh, scoops you up like laundry, and carries you over the worst steps. "Mind you stay dry," she says.

scene_soup_tent.narration: At the high paths, a woman named Marigold gives away soup. DEEP HOLLOW is stitched on her apron. "Whatever sleeps under the mountain could fix the world's rules," she says. "We collect to help it wake." Her little box rattles.

scene_soup_tent_coins.narration: You drop a few coins in the box. They do not clink. Marigold lights up as if you handed her the sun. "It'll wake so gently," she whispers. Your hands feel oddly empty.

scene_soup_tent_refuse.narration: "No, thank you," you say, kindly but firmly. She nods as if she expected it. "Soup's still soup," she says, and ladles you some anyway. You take it, because it is cold up here.

scene_soup_tent_soup.narration: You have the soup. It is very good soup. Marigold says nothing more. When you hand back the bowls, she has somehow already washed them. As you go, the little box rattles once on its own.

choice_rope_bridge.narration: A rope bridge crosses the gorge. Two planks are missing. The sign says MIND THE GAP. Someone added IT IS A BIG GAP. Use a spare plank, the side rope, or a knot you know.

check_bridge_test.narration: The spare planks have a tag: CARRY IT LEVEL. The bridge sways, and so does the plank. Everyone keeps their end steady.

interaction.cue: Everyone lift or lower your end until the plank is level, then carry it to the gap.

onSuccess.narration: Step by careful step, you lay the plank across the gap. On the far side, you add to the sign: WE MINDED IT.

onFailure.narration: The plank lands crooked. It creaks. You say AAH. It turns out to be perfectly fine, just a very dramatic plank.

check_bridge_rope.prompt: Swing hand over hand along the side rope past the missing planks

onSuccess.narration: Hand, hand, hand, and swing your feet onto the far planks. One after another you go over the gap like monkeys, and the bridge hardly sways. A bigfoot coming the other way stops to clap, very slowly, with enormous hands.

onFailure.narration: Halfway along, your arms get tired and you dangle for a moment, like a sock on a clothesline, until the others reach out and pull you in by the belt. Nobody looks down. Well, one person looks down, once, and decides never to do that again.

choice_rope_bridge_knot.narration: Over, under, twist, pull. You tie a spare plank into the gap with the runner's knot. A bigfoot coming the other way tugs it twice and nods. "MossHome knot. Somebody taught you right."

scene_halfway_hut.narration: Past the gorge, an old bigfoot path-keeper keeps a huge visitors' book outside his hut. "Names going up, so I know who to find coming down." The oldest pages are knots. His cake tin has its own tiny visitors' book.

scene_halfway_hut_sign.narration: You sign your names in your best writing. The path-keeper reads them out slowly, as if tasting them. More names are going up this year than ever. "Busy mountain," he says.

check_hut_pages.prompt: Untangle the oldest knotted pages of the visitors' book without pulling a single knot loose

onSuccess.narration: Back and back you turn, past ink, past scratches, to the knots. Each knot is a climber, and the little knots tied on after are what they met on the way up. The commonest one, by far, means CROSS ANIMALS: THROW THEM A SNACK. The path-keeper taps it. "Still good advice," he says. "There are wolves up there today."

onFailure.narration: The knotted pages are like trying to read a knitted sweater. You turn it upside down and it makes even less sense. The path-keeper chuckles, closes the book, and pours you a cup of something hot. "Takes forty years to read those," he says. "I've done thirty-one."

scene_high_paths.narration: Higher up, cinder wolves lie across the path, cross and glowing. They want the warm steps. You want the way north. A narrow ivy ledge runs above them, and a little feeding hollow sits off to one side.

scene_high_paths_hidden.narration: Your bigfoot points to a crack in the cliff. It is an old MossHome path, hidden behind ivy. You squeeze along it right past the wolves' noses. Not one twitches an ear.

check_distract.prompt: Give three cross wolves something more interesting than you

onSuccess.narration: You lob a handful of jerky from your packs down the slope. Three wolves look at each other, then at the jerky, and decide jerky wins.

onFailure.narration: A strip of jerky bounces off a wolf's nose. The wolf does not find this funny.

check_dash.prompt: Dash past three cinder wolves on a narrow cliff path

onSuccess.narration: Over a rope bridge, under a ledge, and gone before a single wolf has finished yawning.

onFailure.narration: The rope bridge squeaks. Six glowing ears turn around.

encounter_wolves.narration: The wolves get up, shake off a shower of sparks, and come down the switchback at you.

onVictory.narration: The wolves decide this path isn't worth it. They lope off downhill, trailing sparks like a sneeze.

onDefeat.narration: The wolves chase you down into a gully. Your packs scatter across the hillside.

check_regroup.prompt: Gather up your scattered packs before it gets dark

onSuccess.narration: You find everything, even the sock nobody wanted back, and climb on, late but whole.

onFailure.narration: You find one pack, half of another, and a hat that is not yours. The light goes while you are still looking, and somewhere above you a wolf grumbles at the mountain as if it has lost something too.

scene_foothills_view.narration: The forest ends at a flat lookout rock. Red foothills roll away toward Mount Red Sky. Down there are the bell towns and the wardens' citadel. You have the stones' oldest secret to carry down to them.

scene_foothills_view_lookout.narration: You scramble up the rock at sunset. You see bell towers, a red stone citadel with lights coming on, and the rush, a glittering line of lanterns crawling toward the mountain.

ending_foothills_rim.narration: You camp at the edge of the foothills, the knot-cord safe in somebody's pocket. All night the mountain grumbles in its sleep, like a giant with a tummy ache.

variants.text: The log crew's ivy lesson got you above the wolves.
The runoff record helped you find the scattered packs.

ending_long_way_round.narration: By the time you find most of your things, it is dark. You come down into the foothills the long way around, a day late and one sock short.

variants.text: The log crew's ivy lesson got you above the wolves.
The runoff record helped you find the scattered packs.

interaction_post_relay.narration: You pass the news cords along the stump while the runner catches her breath. Her legs keep jogging anyway. The cords reach the far runner in time. "Post fee!" she calls, and tosses you three coins.

interaction_cord_knots.narration: While you pack, the runner ties a news cord slowly, so you can follow. Loop, twist, pull, loop. One loose loop looks like a confused spider. "There," she says. "Now the news can find its way."

scene_hut_honeycake.narration: You put two coins in the path-keeper's tin. He hands you a honeycake wrapped in a leaf, like a medal. "Mind the stream past the hut," he says. "A young river drake has moved in."

scene_drake_ford.narration: Up the path, a young river drake slaps waves down the stream. The stepping stones are the only way up. The drake looks like a pony who has just been told to share a bath.

interaction_stones.narration: Slap! A wave rolls down the stream. Slap! Another. The stones are slick, but there is a gap between waves, if you watch for it.

interaction.cue: Wait for the wave to pass, then tap to hop up the stones.

onSuccess.narration: Wave, gap, hop. Wave, gap, hop. You reach the top with dry boots.

onFailure.narration: You hop too early, and a wave fills your boots. The drake looks at you as if you took its towel.

scene_drake_bank.narration: The drake plops itself in the rocky slot above the stones. "Mine," says its snort. Climbers are waiting behind you. It needs a pool of its own so everybody can pass.

encounter_drake.narration: The young drake rears up and slaps the stream, and the slot becomes a splash fight. Move it along before the next climbers get soaked.

scene_drake_shooed.narration: The drake slides into a deep pool beside the path and blows a sulky bubble. Then it coughs up a smooth blue charm and nudges it to you. "Thanks," says its bubble.

scene_drake_splashed.narration: The waves wash you back. The path-keeper hurries up with towels and a tea tray. He bangs the tray until the drake retreats to a side pool. The slot is clear, but there is no charm today.

interaction_camp.narration: The flat rock is bare and a little cold, and the sun is nearly gone. A camp will not make itself. Everybody does a piece.

interaction_falls_logs.narration: Pass the stepping logs up the stair, one to the next. Alone, pass them to the warden. She shows you how an ivy brace steadies a narrow ledge.

interaction.cue: Catch a stepping log and pass it up the stair.

onSuccess.narration: The logs settle into a dry stair. The warden checks your ivy brace.

onFailure.narration: A log rolls the wrong way, and you sit down in the falls with a splash. The flood-warden hauls you out, then drags the logs across herself.

onAssisted.narration: The warden takes the heavy ends while you pass. Together you set the stair and practice the brace.

interaction_ivy_ledge.narration: Use the ivy brace you practiced at the falls. Hold the line tight while one of you guides the way along the ledge. Alone, use the rock post.

interaction.cue: Keep the ivy line taut while the acting hero guides the ledge.

onSuccess.narration: The brace holds. You pass above the wolves without waking them.

onFailure.narration: The ivy slips. You step back onto the wide path, where the wolves are now standing.

onAssisted.narration: A rock fork holds the line for you. You pass above the wolves.

scene_gully_recovery.narration: Your packs have slid down into a damp gully. The wolves stay on the path above. Search the whole hillside, or check the runoff pockets if the flood-warden showed you. A sock sails downhill like a tiny flag.

interaction_runoff_packs.narration: Follow a pack through the fern pockets on your cord. The runoff carries it along. Mark where it settles, then find the rest.

interaction.cue: Follow the pack and choose its final runoff pocket.

onSuccess.narration: You find the packs in the runoff pockets and climb back to the path.

onFailure.narration: You find one pack, half of another, and a hat that is not yours. The light goes while you are still looking.

onAssisted.narration: The water snags a strap on a root. With that help, you gather the packs.

interaction_keeper_pages.narration: The keeper sets a knot key beside the oldest page. Share its clues, and read the old advice in order. His bookmark is tied to his sleeve. It still goes missing.

interaction.cue: Share the knot key and rebuild the keeper's old advice.

options.label: Wait for the animals to turn
Place food away from the path

clues: Place food away from the path before waiting.
Wait for the animals to turn toward the food.
Pass after their noses are pointed away.

onSuccess.narration: The old advice: cross animals, throw them a snack. The keeper shows you a safe feeding hollow by the wolf path.

onFailure.narration: The knots tangle under your fingers. You never finish checking the feeding plan.

onAssisted.narration: The keeper reads the key beside you. Together you find a safe feeding hollow by the wolf path.

scene_checked_snack.narration: You put your food in the feeding hollow the keeper showed you, then wait. The wolves turn, and their noses stay down while you pass. Your supper is gone, but the path is yours.

interaction_camp_response_fire.narration: A small flame crackles on the rock. The blankets are warm, and the tea tastes like a rainy afternoon, in a good way.

interaction_camp_response_blankets.narration: The blankets go down in a soft row. The fire glows, and the tea tastes like a rainy afternoon, in a good way.

interaction_camp_response_tea.narration: Tea steam curls into the dusk. The fire glows, the blankets are warm, and the tea tastes like a rainy afternoon.

voiceGuide.tone: cozy, wise and quietly amazed; a town of librarians who are also a forest, with the mountain grumbling at the edge
forbidden: explaining what the Hollow Gate is

npcVoices.door_archivist: brisk bigfoot archivist; fussy about feet, warm once she decides you matter
npcVoices.oldest_archivist: very old, very slow, a bird lives in his beard; talks to the knot-cords as much as to you
npcVoices.eldest: MossHome elder; mild, sips tea between every sentence, asks to be told second and means it
npcVoices.runner: a MossHome runner; cheerful, out of breath, never stops jogging even while talking
npcVoices.soup_woman: a Deep Hollow Cult member; genuinely kind, soft-spoken, believes every word; kindness first, always, and never menacing
npcVoices.flood_warden: MossHome bigfoot in very tall boots; brisk, practical, has seen every kind of soggy
npcVoices.path_keeper: old bigfoot who keeps the halfway hut on the high paths; slow, kind, proud of his visitors' book
npcVoices.young_gatherer: a young dragonling gatherer; insists she is not lost, knows the one rule by heart, braver than she feels

interaction_post_relay.narration: A runner hands you knotted news cords. Pass them along the stump to the runner at the far end. "Out of legs!" she pants, still jogging on two perfectly good ones.

interaction.cue: Catch the bundle of cords, then pass it down the line.

onSuccess.narration: The cords fly from hand to hand and reach the far runner with a whole breath to spare. "Post fee!" she calls, and tosses you three coins, jingling. Then she jogs off with the news, still jogging.

onFailure.narration: One bundle lands in a puddle, and two cords tie themselves to a runner's boot. She hops, laughs, and untangles it. "The news will get there," she says. "News always does."

onAssisted.narration: A runner jogs in between you and takes every other throw. The cords reach the far end in good time, and a runner tosses you three coins, jingling, for the help.

interaction_cord_knots.narration: The runner holds up a record cord. Watch the loops, then echo them. "The record likes to know you can." A loose loop resembles a confused spider. The runner asks it to behave.

interaction.cue: Watch the knots light up, then tie them back in the same order.

onSuccess.narration: Loop, twist, pull, loop. Your cord comes out exactly like hers, and the runner whoops. "Not one wrong knot!" she says. "I will tell the record."

onFailure.narration: Your knots come out in a tangle shaped like a very confused spider. The runner unties it with one finger. "Close," she says kindly. "I will do the last loop for you."

check_chair_sit.narration: The small archivist with the string waves you over. "It will not stand up for one person," she says. "Somebody sits and leans, and everybody pushes on the back. The chair has to feel the whole group."

interaction.cue: Friends push the chair upright while someone sits and leans back.

onSuccess.narration: You sit and lean back hard. With a long creak the chair comes upright, and holds, and holds, and the moment you stand up it leans straight back again, slowly, like a sunflower turning. The small archivist writes on her sign, under FILE OPENED: STILL OPEN.

onFailure.narration: You sit, and lean, and the chair politely tips you out onto the moss, the way you would tip out a cat that has sat on your homework. The small archivist laughs so hard she drops her string. "It does that to everybody," she says. "Even the Eldest. Especially the Eldest."

interaction_camp.narration: The flat rock at the edge of the foothills is bare and a little cold, and the sun is nearly gone. A camp will not make itself. Everybody does a piece of it.

interaction.cue: Everybody add something to the camp until it feels cozy.

options.label: Light a little fire
options.reaction: A small flame crackles on the rock.

options.label: Roll out the blankets
options.reaction: The blankets go down in a soft row.

options.label: Warm the moss tea
options.reaction: Tea steam curls up into the dusk.

stages: The fire settles down to a glow.

onSuccess.narration: The fire glows, the blankets are warm, and the tea tastes like a rainy afternoon, in a good way.

onFailure.narration: The fire is a little smoky and the blankets are a little crooked, but the camp will do.
